targetEra.scene: ordinary midsummer Japanese new-town apartment exterior

historicalBasis.claim: A rooftop fishbone/Yagi receiving silhouette is appropriate evidence for the year-2000 target because Japanese terrestrial television remained analogue until the 2011 switchover; VHF receiving arrays were part of the analogue-era installation vocabulary.

Analogue-era Japanese rooftop reception commonly used Yagi-style antennas, with VHF used for major analogue terrestrial channels and UHF also used for regional channels; this pass therefore models separate large-VHF and compact-UHF arrays rather than a modern flat design antenna.

A Japanese communal-reception product reference documents hot-dip-galvanized 40A antenna masts at approximately 48.6 mm outside diameter and 3.0-4.0 m lengths. This is used only as a dimensional/manufacturing comparator for the modeled 48 mm x 3.28 m mast, not as a claim that the exact current/discontinued product was installed in 2000.

assembly.reasoning: Use one maintained communal rooftop service assembly as a period marker. Do not randomize manufactured apartment modules or scatter nostalgic props. The assembly must have a legible roof-to-ballast-to-rail-to-stay/collar-to-mast load path, a cable path and frequency-dependent antenna proportions.

location.edgeSetbackIntent: kept inward from the parapet so the mounting reads as maintained communal infrastructure

components.name: non_penetrating_ballast_base
components.mounting: gravity ballast supporting paired galvanized base rails; no unexplained roof membrane penetration
components.interfaces: block-to-roof bearing surface, block-to-rail compression/contact, mast saddle at paired rail center, stay-foot plates at rail ends
components.geometryVsMaterial: block mass, rail thickness, saddle, stay feet and gaps are geometry; aggregate/pinhole response belongs to material microdetail

components.name: galvanized_mast
components.manufacture: round steel tube, hot-dip galvanized after fabrication
components.mounting: lower saddle plus four-way stayed collar transfer lateral mast load into paired ballast rails
components.interfaces: mast-saddle clamp, mast-stay collar, boom-to-mast clamps, coax tied alongside mast

components.name: four_way_mast_stay_system
components.manufacture: galvanized tubular compression/tension stays fixed to formed rail-foot plates and a clamped mast collar
components.mounting: two stays land on each of the two ballast rails near opposite ends; four upper nodes terminate at collar lugs around the mast
components.interfaces: stay-to-foot plate, foot plate-to-base rail, stay-to-collar lug, collar-to-mast
components.orientation: four triangulated diagonals around the mast; do not collapse to a decorative vertical support
components.aging: zinc dulling and runoff concentration may occur at clamp/foot interfaces; intact galvanized surfaces must not receive arbitrary orange rust
components.geometryVsMaterial: all stays, collar, feet and near-camera lugs are geometry; zinc spangle, oxidation and fine runoff variation are material/weathering response

components.name: vhf_yagi_array
components.manufacture: tubular boom and transverse conductive elements with dielectric feed enclosure
components.mounting: boom clamped to mast around 2.93 m above roof
components.orientation: elements transverse to boom; physically larger than UHF array

components.name: uhf_yagi_array
components.manufacture: compact tubular boom and transverse conductive elements with dielectric feed enclosure
components.mounting: boom clamped to mast around 2.34 m above roof
components.orientation: elements transverse to boom; visibly more compact than VHF array

components.name: coax_and_roof_junction
components.mounting: coax follows mast downward with six explicit UV-resistant mast clips in LOD0/1, then turns into a short roof conduit and weather-resistant junction box
components.interfaces: feed-box cable exit, cable-to-mast clips, roof conduit, enclosure entry
components.geometryVsMaterial: cable route, clip bridges and enclosure depth are geometry; UV chalking and fine molding/extrusion texture belong to material

materials.albedoLinearIntent: neutral slightly cool zinc-grey, no painted highlight
materials.specularF0: conductor response; do not force dielectric F0
materials.microstructure: subtle zinc-spangle/rolled-tube irregularity; must not become a visible tiled camouflage pattern
materials.wetness: benchmark is dry; rain-wet state would primarily lower roughness rather than darken via painted gloss
materials.uvAging: mild oxidation dulling only; no orange ferrous rust on intact zinc surface
materials.angularFresnelResponse: real metallic edge/grazing response from the shader/environment; no baked white stripe

materials.albedoLinearIntent: dark charcoal rather than absolute black
materials.microstructure: fine injection-molded plastic texture below silhouette scale
materials.uvAging: slight chalking/desaturation on upward/sunward faces only
materials.angularFresnelResponse: weak dielectric grazing lift, never mirror-like

materials.albedoLinearIntent: very dark neutral PVC with enough value to retain cylindrical form
materials.uvAging: subtle upper-surface fading, no random white speckles

materials.albedoLinearIntent: weathered neutral warm-grey; no AO or contact shadow painted into albedo
materials.microstructure: fine aggregate, pores and form/mold variation at millimetric scale
materials.wetness: dry benchmark; no global wet gloss

allowed: UV dulling/chalking on upward or sunward polymer surfaces
zinc oxidation/dulling on exposed galvanized members
localized runoff concentration below collar, lug and rail-foot interfaces
fine accumulated grime at ballast-to-roof and rail-to-ballast contact recesses
forbidden: random rust decals without exposed ferrous substrate
uniform wet gloss in the dry benchmark
damage or staining that implies disaster/reconstruction

lodPolicy.lod0: 8 VHF elements + 14 UHF elements + feed boxes + coax path/clips + four ballast blocks + four mast stays + collar + stay feet/lugs
lodPolicy.lod1: 6 VHF + 8 UHF elements while retaining feed/cable/clips/base/stays/collar and simplified near-camera attachment hardware
lodPolicy.lod2: 4 VHF + 4 UHF elements; preserve two-frequency silhouette plus all four stays, collar and ballast load path; omit sub-pixel feet/lugs/clips
lodPolicy.lod3: 2 VHF + 2 UHF elements plus mast/booms/base/four stays/collar; structural silhouette only
lodPolicy.antiPopRequirement: actual 4K motion evidence is required; source-side cross-fade and persistent stay geometry are readiness only

lookdevBrief.frontal: At native 4K the roofline should gain a restrained late-analogue-era infrastructure silhouette. Large VHF and smaller UHF arrays must read as two engineered scales, not one decorative comb. Four-way stayed mast support should read as infrastructure without becoming visually dominant.
lookdevBrief.oblique: Boom depth, element spacing, paired ballast rails, four diagonal stays, mast collar, saddle and cable path should demonstrate a continuous installation load path. No stay or element should visibly float or interpenetrate another hero part.
lookdevBrief.grazingLight: Galvanized mast/stays/rails should develop narrow environment-driven metallic highlights while remaining rough; black feed boxes/coax stay dielectric. Concrete ballast remains broad and matte. No highlight may be painted into albedo.
100PercentCropChecks: LOD transition or shimmer if motion evidence becomes available

visualGateMapping.periodAccuracySceneAuthenticity: primary expected benefit; year-2000 roofline receives a historically coherent analogue receiving system rather than generic modern flat antennas
visualGateMapping.geometryConstructionFidelity: visible load path from roof ballast to rails/saddle/stays/collar/mast/booms/elements and explicit cable restraint
visualGateMapping.materialPBR: bare galvanized zinc is metallic; feed enclosure/PVC/concrete are dielectric
visualGateMapping.weatheringContextCausality: runoff, UV aging and zinc dulling are tied to exposure and installation interfaces
visualGateMapping.temporalLod: four explicit cross-faded LOD levels preserve the mast support silhouette; runtime evidence still mandatory

automaticFailIfObserved: modern flat/design terrestrial antenna replacing the year-2000 analogue Yagi silhouette without documented context
Unity primitive placeholder mesh visible in benchmark framing
galvanized metal treated as painted dielectric or ABS/PVC/concrete treated as metal
painted or baked white antenna highlights
floating mast base, floating stay endpoint or unexplained roof penetration

renderVerification.instruction: Do not award Period Accuracy, Geometry, Material, Weathering or Temporal points from source configuration alone.
